correctness.rationale: For all n>=4, f in {0,...,n} with n-f even, and disjoint comparisons j-i>=2, the weighted Littlewood/RSK identity supplies label-independent counts of one and two forced ascents. The two-color Burnside computation gives A2=(I_nf-I_(n-2,f)+I_(n-2,f-2))/2 and 4A22=I_nf-2I_(n-2,f)+3I_(n-4,f)+2I_(n-2,f-2)-2I_(n-4,f-2)+I_(n-4,f-4). Dividing by I_nf and using exact falling-factorial ratios reproduces Cov=-(n-f)B_n(f)/(2n^2(n-3)(n-2)(n-1)^2), B_n(f)=(2n-3)f^3-nf^2+n^2f-n^2(n-2), as an independently factored sympy identity. B_n(0)<0, B_n(n-2)>0, and B_n prime has discriminant 4n^2(10-6n)<0, giving exactly one positive root; f=n is deterministic. Rescale f=cn^(2/3) to obtain n^2 Cov -> (1-2c^3)/2 and root/n^(2/3)->2^(-1/3). Independently recursively generated all involutions n=4..9 (3728 total), checked 24 conditional fixed-point classes with exact Fraction single and disjoint ascent probabilities and covariance, and verified roots numerically at n=4,6,10,50,100,1000,100000. Finite tests are corroborative only.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration through n=9 is not the infinite proof; the universal step uses the cited Littlewood/RSK identity and exact Burnside argument.

value.rationale: The conditioned involution conjugacy class is a standard natural probability model, and disjoint descent correlations are a meaningful local-dependence invariant used in variance/normality analysis. The theorem identifies a complete size-uniform one-crossing positive-to-negative phase diagram and nonobvious mesoscopic scale f~n^(2/3) with explicit scaled profile; neither the sign pattern nor transition scale is visible from a fixed-positive-fraction central limit theorem. The derivation is more than a renaming, raw coefficient table, or trivial finite evaluation, even though it is an exact consequence of classical enumeration.
residual_risks: This result is a sharp structural corollary of existing generating functions, not a wholly new distribution theorem or a CLT.
No claim about overlapping descent positions or all higher correlations; critical-window covariance is O(n^-2).

limitations: The proved model is fixed-point-conditioned uniform involutions, not unrestricted random involutions; f and n parity constrained.
Nonadjacent comparisons only (j-i>=2); adjacent and higher-order event laws are outside the claim.
The classic exact fixed-point-weighted descent-set enumerator fully covers underlying distribution data; priority belongs only to claimed derived sign/scale property, qualified by relevant sources.
